findings.issue: The product feature describes a default loss guarantee (DLG) cover of up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio, which exceeds the RBI's cap of five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time.
findings.doc_evidence: CredBridge will cover losses up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio.
findings.fix: Reduce the DLG cover from 10% to 5% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio to comply with RBI's cap.
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph explicitly states that the total amount of DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time. The product feature describes a DLG cover of up to 10% of the total amount disbursed in each quarterly portfolio, which exceeds the RBI's cap of five per cent. Therefore, the feature violates the RBI regulation.

findings.feature: Default Loss Guarantee (3. Form of DLG)
findings.issue: The DLG arrangements are not backed by an explicit and legally enforceable contract between the RE and the DLG provider. The product feature does not mention the existence of such a contract, which is a mandatory requirement under [DLD2025:21(i)].
findings.doc_evidence: The DLG will be given as a corporate guarantee from CredBridge's parent company, rather than cash or a bank guarantee.
findings.fix: Draft and execute an explicit and legally enforceable contract between the RE and the DLG provider, and include it in the product documentation.
findings.verifier_note: The product feature does not explicitly mention the existence of a legally enforceable contract between the RE and the DLG provider, which is a mandatory requirement under [DLD2025:21(i)]. Therefore, the feature fails to meet the requirement of having an explicit and legally enforceable contract.

findings.feature: Default Loss Guarantee (3. Form of DLG)
findings.issue: The RE is allowed to invoke the DLG only after a loan has been overdue for 180 days, which exceeds the maximum overdue period of 120 days specified in [DLD2025:26(i)].
findings.doc_evidence: Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 180 days.
findings.fix: Adjust the overdue period for invoking DLG from 180 days to 120 days as specified in [DLD2025:26(i)].
findings.verifier_note: The RBI paragraph [DLD2025:26(i)] states that RE shall invoke DLG within a maximum overdue period of 120 days, unless the loan dues are made good by the borrower before that. The product feature states that Coastal Finance will invoke the DLG once a loan has been overdue for 180 days, which exceeds the 120-day limit specified in the RBI paragraph. Therefore, the feature violates the requirement of invoking DLG within 120 days.

findings.feature: Default Loss Guarantee (5. Board policy and due diligence)
findings.issue: The product feature states that CredBridge gives an auditor-certified declaration of its total DLG outstanding and past default rates at signing and at every renewal. summary: The compliance review of the Partnership Term Sheet for the Coastal Finance x CredBridge (DLG arrangement) identified several non-compliance issues with the RBI rules. The product feature exceeds the RBI's cap on DLG cover, lacks an explicit and legally enforceable contract between the RE and DLG provider, allows invocation of DLG after an overdue period exceeding the prescribed limit, and fails to meet the requirements for DLG provider eligibility and declaration details.
